title: Shrink Sheet: Working Out the Bushels a Conditioning Loss Takes Off
content:
The shrink is taken on the bushels the most recent conditioning charge was raised on, on the points that charge shows, and at the handling shrink percentage the programme sets for each point. This sheet covers Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The quantity taken off

The bushels taken off are the bushels the shrink is taken on, multiplied by the points it is taken on and by the handling shrink percentage the programme sets for each point, that product divided by one hundred and rounded to two decimal places.

The percentage is carried to three decimal places before it is applied.

## Worked line, on hypothetical figures

Take an agreement whose programme sets a handling shrink percentage of 0.55 for each point. The most recent conditioning charge on the storage account was raised on 9200 bushels and shows 3.4 points.

1. The bushels the shrink is taken on are 9200, being those the most recent conditioning charge was raised on.
2. The points are 3.4, being those that charge shows.
3. The percentage carried to three decimal places is 0.550.
4. Nine thousand two hundred bushels multiplied by 3.4 points multiplied by 0.550 is 17204.00, and divided by one hundred that is 172.04.
5. Rounded to two decimal places, 172.04 bushels come off what is held in store.

## A second worked line

On the same programme, a conditioning charge raised on 1500 bushels showing 0.8 points gives 1500 multiplied by 0.8 multiplied by 0.550, which is 660.00, divided by one hundred that is 6.60, and rounded to two decimal places 6.60 bushels come off.

## Notes

**Is the quantity a charge?** It is not. The line carries bushels and no money at all.

**What is divided by one hundred?** The product of the bushels, the points and the percentage, the percentage being expressed as a percentage rather than as a fraction.
